title: Fill in the dead sensors
prompt:
Some of pod 3's inlet sensors have died, but you have a POD of the healthy field from last month: its `mean` (p,) and its first k `modes` as unit-length rows (k, p).

Write `fill_missing(X, observed, mean, modes)`. `X` has shape (n, p), one snapshot per row, with NaN in the columns of the dead sensors; `observed` is a boolean array (p,), True where the sensor works. For each snapshot, find the mode coefficients that best fit the **working** sensors in the least-squares sense (Lesson 3 again), then estimate the dead sensors as mean + coefficients · modes. Return a copy of `X` with the dead columns filled and the working sensors' readings unchanged.

Raise `ValueError` if fewer sensors work than there are modes. Solve every snapshot at once with one call to `np.linalg.lstsq` (it accepts many right-hand sides as columns), with no loops.
hints: Each snapshot is approximately mean + a₁φ₁ + … + a_kφ_k. You can't compute the aᵢ by projecting the full snapshot, because some entries are missing. What can you do with only the working rows of that equation?

Keep only the working sensors: A = modes[:, observed].T has shape (n_working, k), and B = (X[:, observed] − mean[observed]).T holds one snapshot per column. Solving A a = B in the least-squares sense gives every snapshot's coefficients at once. The modes are no longer orthonormal once rows are removed, so projecting with modes @ x gives biased coefficients; least squares doesn't care.

if observed.sum() < len(modes): raise ValueError(...). coef = np.linalg.lstsq(modes[:, observed].T, (X[:, observed] - mean[observed]).T, rcond=None)[0]; est = mean + coef.T @ modes; out = X.copy(); out[:, ~observed] = est[:, ~observed]; return out.

misconceptions.gappy-projection: With rows missing, the modes aren't orthonormal on the remaining sensors, so dot products don't give the coefficients. Fit them by least squares on the working sensors.
misconceptions.pca-needs-centering: The modes describe deviations from the mean field: subtract the mean before fitting and add it back afterwards.
